title: Large Bets and Stock Market Crashes
one_line: Market-microstructure 'invariance' predicts price impact of large forced sales far better than conventional wisdom: e.g., 1987 portfolio insurance sales (67% of ADV) → predicted −16.8% vs actual −32%; SocGen 2008 −10.8% vs −9.4%; aggregate-market demand elasticity ≈ 0.01, so even ~1-3% of daily volume sold quickly moves index markets materially.

findings.statement: Impact ∝ (dollar volume)^(1/3) × (vol)^(4/3) × order size / volume; k = 5 calibrated on 400k portfolio transitions.
1929 −46% predicted vs −25% actual; 1987 −17% vs −32%; 2010 flash crash −0.6% vs −5.1% (speed amplified).
Faster execution increases temporary impact → V-shaped moves.

why.pattern: Forced, fast selling relative to market depth creates outsized temporary impact that partly reverses.

tradable_edge: No strategy. Supports the flow-to-depth logic of letf_flow_to_depth_last_hour_es and the V-shaped reversal logic of forced_selling_flush_fade_es.
